battle.name: 金鄉之戰
battle.brief: 隋文帝開皇年間第一次大舉征高句麗，五十餘萬大軍分水陸兩路北上，陸軍沿遼西走廊推進至遼西南境的金鄉，連日大雨、士卒疲病、糧運不繼，兵鋒止步於此；高句麗遣使請降，隋軍班師而還，本卡以埃及月牙劍作早期冷兵器的對照。

kit.name: 埃及月牙劍
kit.history: 外彎的單刃劍，砍下去不用拔。它比直劍更早出現在埃及人的手上。

countries: 交戰的兩方，是剛剛取代南朝、統一了中原的隋朝，與控制朝鮮半島北部以及遼東的高句麗。隋文帝楊堅在開皇年間集結的遠征軍，由宗室諸王掛名總領，行軍元帥與行軍總監分統水陸大軍：陸軍沿遼西走廊自幽州一路東北行，水軍則自山東萊州、北海一帶入海，循海濱北航，兩線的目標都是遼東治襄平與平壤。前線統兵的老將于仲文負責突前與追擊，行軍總監宇文愷總攬舟楫、糧秣、堰渠與屯駐工程，是把五十餘萬人的遠征真正推動起來的關鍵人物。高句麗方面由國王高元坐鎮平壤，遣大將乙支文德率高句麗本部兵與靺鞨等外族部落的兵馬迎戰，同時以遣使請降的外交手段拖延時間。這不是兩國傾國全面交鋒，而是一場中央王朝以傾國之力對邊疆政權施加的懲罰性進攻，交戰雙方的目標、補給條件與地理距離都相差懸殊，勝負在開戰前便已埋下伏筆。
countriesEn: The two sides in this conflict were the Sui dynasty, which had just replaced the Chen house and unified the Central Plain, and Goguryeo, which controlled northern Korea and the Liaodong region. The expedition fielded by Emperor Wen of Sui during the Kaihuang era was nominally commanded by princes of the imperial clan, while a marshal and an overall director of the expedition divided the army into a land force and a water force: the land column marched north-east from Youzhou along the Liaoxi corridor, while the water force entered the sea from the coast of Shandong around Laizhou and Beihai, sailed northward along the littoral, and both columns aimed at Xiangping, the seat of Liaodong, and at Pyongyang. The veteran general Yu Zhongwen commanded the vanguard and the pursuit, while the overall director Yuwen Kai took charge of the warships, the grain, the dams and the encampments, and was the man who actually made an expedition of more than half a million men possible. On the Goguryeo side, King Go-won held Pyongyang, sent the general Iji Winde with Goguryeo’s own troops and with contingents drawn from tribes such as the Mohe to meet the invaders, and at the same time stalled for time by sending envoys to sue for peace. This was never a general war between two fully committed states; it was a punitive thrust by a central dynasty throwing its whole strength at a frontier polity, and the disparity in objectives, in supply and in distance was so great that the outcome was already decided before the first clash.
people: 核心人物是隋文帝楊堅。自陳朝覆亡、中原歸於一統之後，他便把恢復漢魏舊疆、威懾北亞列國列為基本國策，金鄉之役正是這一取向的第一次實踐：下詔募兵、發出師令、規定進退節奏，都出於他的聖裁。統軍的于仲文是北周舊將，久經邊事，多次請以速戰為上；行軍總監宇文愷專司舟楫、水利與糧道，是把五十餘萬大軍的遠征推上路的工程總負責人。宗室方面，晉王楊廣、齊王楊秀、越王楊諒等分統各路，掛帥印而未盡親至前線，實際指揮仍歸幕府。高句麗方面，國王高元坐居平壤，主持應戰與和談的雙線應對；大將乙支文德率兵在薩水一線佈防，遣使請降與堅守不出之間的分寸拿捏，出自其幕府之手。隋文帝事後以大軍無功而還、虛耗糧餉為由，一度收繫問罪於仲文等將領，隨後又因邊防實況與其才略重新起用，顯示這場遠征在隋廷內部同樣引起震動與爭議。
peopleEn: The central figure is Emperor Wen of Sui, Yang Jian. After the fall of the Chen house and the reunification of the Central Plain, he made the recovery of the old Han and Wei frontiers and the intimidation of the northern powers a cornerstone of state policy, and the Jinxiang campaign was the first practical expression of that policy: the call for levies, the order to march and the tempo of advance and retreat were all his own decisions. Yu Zhongwen, who led the host, was a veteran of Northern Zhou who had served on the frontier for years and repeatedly pressed for a quick decision. Yuwen Kai, the overall director of the expedition, handled ships, waterworks and the grain line, and was the engineer who actually got a host of more than half a million men moving. On the imperial side among the princes, Yang Guang of Jin, Yang Xiu of Qi and Yang Liang of Yue held nominal command of the several columns without coming in person to the front, so that the real work of command remained with the staffs. In Goguryeo, King Go-won sat at Pyongyang and managed both the conduct of the war and the diplomacy of surrender, while the general Iji Winde held the line at the Salsu river and set the exact measure of the Goguryeo reply, offering submission through envoys while refusing to give ground. Afterwards Emperor Wen, angered that so vast an army had returned empty-handed and had wasted the revenue, had the commanders such as Yu Zhongwen detained and questioned, only to put them back into service when the frontier situation and their own abilities demanded it; the expedition, in other words, shook the Sui court as well as the Goguryeo court.
kits: 本卡兵器是埃及月牙劍：古埃及新王國時期步兵所用的外彎單刃短刀，以青銅刃配木柄，砍擊之後不必像直劍那樣反覆拔插。須說清楚的是，這件兵器與隋軍毫無關係，隋朝軍中不可能出現月牙劍；把它放上卡面，是當作早期文明短兵器的對照樣本，用來衡量這場戰役真正用到的刀類裝備。隋軍的冷兵器主力是環首刀與直刀，長兵器以馬槊、方天畫戟與長槍為主，遠射以弓弩為核心，攻城則倚靠雲梯、撞車、蒙衝、飛雲、擲石車與巢車一類器械，並備拒馬、鐵蒺藜、鹿角等障礙；水軍方面由宇文愷主持造舟，附設水攻與堰渠設施。軍中戰馬與輜重馬數量龐大，糧食靠車牛、海運與陸運輸送。高句麗軍裝備以鐵甲、弓箭、槍刀為主，善於騎射，並倚靠山城、森林與木柵寨作縱深抵抗。兩造都沒有火器，其戰爭本質仍由青銅與鐵器時代的刀、槊、弩以及投射型攻城器械決定，勝負落在刀刃的硬度、槊的長度、弩的射程與器械的數量上。
kitsEn: The weapon on this card is the khopesh, the outward-curving single-edged short sword used by infantry in the New Kingdom period of ancient Egypt, with a bronze blade set in a wooden grip, which could be swung without the need to wrench it back out of a body the way a straight sword had to be. It should be said plainly that this weapon had nothing to do with the Sui army, and no khopesh could ever have appeared in a Sui camp; it is placed on the card as a comparative sample of early cold weaponry, a yardstick against which the blades actually used in this campaign can be measured. The Sui cold arsenal consisted above all of ring-pommel and straight swords, with long weapons such as the horse lance, the halberd and the long spear, and with bows and crossbows as the core of its missile arm; for siege work it relied on scaling ladders, battering rams, covered shock carriages, tall siege towers, stone-throwers and observation platforms, and it carried chevaux-de-frise, iron caltrops and abatis as obstacles. On the water side Yuwen Kai directed the construction of the fleet and added water-attack and dam works to the plan. Horses of war and pack animals were very numerous, and grain moved by cart and draught animal, by sea and by land. The Goguryeo force was armed with iron armour, bows and arrows, spears and swords, was strong in mounted archery, and made its depth out of hill forts, forests and timber stockades. Neither side had gunpowder weapons: the contest was decided by bronze and iron blades, lance reach, crossbow range and the sheer number of siege engines.
tactics: 隋軍的戰術是典型的水陸並進、分進合擊：以幽州為基地的陸軍沿遼西走廊東北行，沿途取城為堡、步步為營；以山東出發的水軍沿海北上，兩軍期在遼東、平壤會師。進攻次序是先取遼東重鎮襄平，再圖樂浪，最後直指平壤。作戰中以步兵方陣居中、騎兵兩翼護衛，攻城時集中使用雲梯、撞車與擲石器，並以填土、覆土、築台等手段對付壕塹。真正決定戰局的，是補給線與天候：五十餘萬大軍加上倍量的運糧民夫，糧道橫跨數千里，軍行至遼東金鄉一帶時連日大雨，道路泥濘，士卒疲病、糧運不繼，攻勢遂停。高句麗一方避免正面會戰，退守險要、堅壁清野、遊騎襲擾糧道，並在薩水一線以步騎混合的伏擊消耗隋軍前鋒；最後以遣使請降、稱臣的姿態換取隋軍退兵，而隋軍一經退去，邊線即恢復原狀。
tacticsEn: The Sui method was classic parallel advance by land and sea, with the two columns intended to converge: the land column, based on Youzhou, marched north-east along the Liaoxi corridor, taking towns and turning them into fortified depots as it went, while the water force sailed north from Shandong, the two arms expecting to join at Liaodong and Pyongyang. The order of operations was to take the great stronghold of Xiangping in Liaodong first, then reach for Lelang, and only then turn on Pyongyang. In action the infantry formed the centre of the line with cavalry on the wings, and siege work concentrated scaling ladders, rams and stone-throwers, while trenches were answered by filling them in, by revetting and by building up earthen platforms. What actually decided the campaign was the supply line and the weather: with more than half a million men and a matching complement of drivers and porters, the grain road ran across thousands of li, and when the army reached the Jinxiang area of Liaodong it met with days of heavy rain; the roads turned to mud, the men sickened and tired, the grain train fell behind, and the offensive stopped there. Goguryeo avoided a general engagement, withdrew to strong ground, refused to be drawn out, sent light horse to harry the supply columns, and used mixed infantry and cavalry ambushes along the Salsu to bleed the Sui vanguard. Finally, offering surrender and submission through envoys bought the withdrawal of the Sui army, and once the army was gone the frontier line went back to where it had been.
data: 關於兵力，正史記載的出師人數在五十萬上下，通行本《資治通鑑》作五十一萬五千人，《隋書》一系則概稱五十餘萬，水陸分統而不列細帳；高句麗方面投入遼東方向的兵員，傳世文獻只作概說，可以確定的是乙支文德一路混合了高句麗本部兵與靺鞨等外族部落兵，量級在十萬上下。行程方面，部隊自正月下詔、二月出師，到盛夏才抵達金鄉，耗時約四個月；金鄉距遼東城襄平尚有數百里，水陸兩線之間的距離更以千里計。糧秣可以估算：按每兵每日二升計，五十萬大軍一日即耗糧約十萬石，若計入運糧民夫、馬匹飼料與沿途損耗，實際需求更高，而自關中、洛陽運糧至遼東，車牛與民夫的消耗又倍於此數。關於損耗，傳世史籍只概稱班師時士卒疲病者眾，傷亡總數各家記載互有出入，通行說法是以萬計乃至逾十萬，但無名籍可校，故此只記其量級而不列確數。
dataEn: On troop strength, the historical record puts the army that marched out at around half a million men, the received text of the Zizhi Tongjian giving 515,000 while the Sishu and its tradition speak generally of more than 500,000, with the land and water columns carried separately and no detailed returns; for the Goguryeo side the sources give only a general figure, and what can be established is that Iji Winde’s command mixed Goguryeo’s own troops with contingents from outside peoples such as the Mohe, on the order of a hundred thousand. On distance and time, the call went out in the first month, the host marched in the second, and it was not until high summer that the column reached Jinxiang, a passage of about four months; Jinxiang still lay several hundred li short of Xiangping, the seat of Liaodong, and the two lines were a thousand li apart. The grain can be computed: at two sheng per man per day, half a million men consume on the order of 100,000 shi of grain every day, and the real requirement was higher once drivers, fodder and transport losses were counted, while moving grain from Guanzhong and Luoyang to Liaodong cost cart animals and porters several times that again. As for losses, the records only say generally that many of the men were sick and exhausted on the march home; the totals differ from source to source, the common account being that casualties ran into the tens of thousands or even above a hundred thousand, but no muster roll exists to check it, so only the order of magnitude is recorded here rather than a precise figure.
cause: 這場戰爭的直接起因，是隋文帝與高句麗之間的朝貢關係破裂。開皇年間隋朝先後遣使往聘，高句麗王元表面接受冊封與使節來往，卻不依詔書入朝、不按期修貢，隋廷視之為對中央王朝的輕慢；同期高句麗在東北整合靺鞨等部落、收容北來流人，與北方突厥往來密切，使隋朝無法忽視其側翼地位。更深層的原因是隋文帝本人的邊疆觀：北周分裂時北方邊族得以坐大，陳朝覆亡後全國歸於一統，朝廷上下普遍認為必須趁新造之勢掃除北患、重建漢代以來的邊界秩序。開皇十七年前後高句麗仍不奉詔、邊警頻傳，隋文帝遂下令大舉東征，試圖以一次遠征解決遼東與朝鮮半島北部的問題，恢復樂浪、玄菟等舊郡的實際控制。徵兵與備戰自關中、河北、山東同時展開，役前外交斡旋亦未見效果，戰端遂開。
causeEn: The immediate cause of the war was the breakdown of tributary relations between Emperor Wen and Goguryeo. During the Kaihuang era the Sui court sent envoys south and east more than once, and King Go-won of Goguryeo outwardly accepted investiture and the exchange of embassies, yet did not come to court as the edict required and did not render tribute at the appointed times; the Sui court read this as a slight offered to the central dynasty. At the same time Goguryeo was consolidating the Mohe and other tribes in the north-east, taking in refugees from the north, and keeping up close contacts with the Turks to its north, so that the Sui could not treat its position on the flank as negligible. The deeper cause lay in Emperor Wen’s own view of the frontier: while the north had been divided under Northern Zhou the northern peoples had grown strong, and now that the fall of Chen had reunited the country the court at large held that the moment had come to sweep away the northern menace and restore the frontier order of Han times. When Goguryeo still refused to obey the edict and frontier alarms continued to come in around the seventeenth year of Kaihuang, Emperor Wen ordered the great eastern expedition, hoping that a single campaign would settle Liaodong and northern Korea and restore effective control over the old commanderies of Lelang and Xuantu. Levies were raised and preparations made simultaneously in Guanzhong, Hebei and Shandong, the diplomatic attempts made before the campaign produced no result, and the war began.
impact: 直接影響是隋朝第一次大征高句麗以無功而還。五十餘萬大軍往返消耗了關中與河北的丁口、馬匹與糧秣，府兵戰力與民力都付出代價，國庫與民戶承受沉重壓力，邊境形勢未見改變。更長遠的影響在戰略取捨：隋文帝自此不再急於東征，改以靜觀其變的辦法，任高句麗全力與北方突厥爭強，把壓力轉給對手；隋朝則把重心轉向鞏固長城防線、經營河西，並在遼東、幽州一帶屯田設鎮，唐代營州、遼東都督府一系的軍鎮格局正是在這一背景下成形。高句麗則爭取到喘氣時間，趁隋軍退去之際重整北方防務，把主力轉向對付突厥。此役亦是隋唐兵器史的一個節點：遠征軍仍以環首刀、馬槊、弓弩與攻城器械為核心，早期那種外彎單刃短刀早已退居象徵地位，而唐代制度化的橫刀、儀刀則在此後數十年內接續成形；中原王朝與東北亞的兵器交流亦循海陸兩線更形密切。
impactEn: The direct effect of the campaign was that the Sui’s first great invasion of Goguryeo came home with nothing. More than half a million men moving out and back consumed the manpower, the horses and the grain of Guanzhong and Hebei; the fighting strength of the fubing and the labour of the countryside were both spent, the treasury and the households bore the weight of it, and the frontier was no better than before. The more far-reaching consequence lay in a change of strategic appetite: Emperor Wen did not press east again in a hurry, and instead watched and waited, letting Goguryeo expend itself against the Turks to the north and passing the pressure on to its opponent; the Sui turned instead to strengthening the Great Wall lines, to the western corridor and to garrisoning and farming Liaodong and Youzhou, the shape of the Tang-era military prefectures of Yingzhou and Liaodong taking form against that background. Goguryeo, for its part, bought breathing space, reorganized its northern defences while the Sui army was withdrawing, and swung its main strength towards the Turks. The campaign is also a hinge in the military-history of weapons for the Sui and the Tang: the expeditionary army was still built around ring-pommel swords, horse lances, bows and crossbows and siege engines, the early outward-curving single-edged short sword had long since sunk to the level of a symbol, and the regulated straight swords and ceremonial blades of the Tang were still a matter of decades away; the exchange of weapons between the Central Plain and northeastern Asia also grew closer along the two lines, sea and land.
result: 就軍事結果而言，傳世史籍沒有記錄隋軍在此役中攻下遼東城或平壤的城邑，隋軍主力止步於金鄉一帶，攻勢因雨、疲、糧三事而中止，實際戰果近乎空白。高句麗方面，乙支文德指揮的防禦與高元的和談同時奏效：遣使請降、稱臣的姿態換得隋軍班師，而隋軍一經退去，邊境線即恢復原狀，高句麗得以騰出兵力應付北方突厥。隋廷內部則因勞師無功而震動，統軍將領一度被收繫問罪，隨後又因邊防實需重新起用；此役後隋文帝不再急於東征，但也沒有放棄東征的準備，直至其晚年，國力與邊患的累積終在隋煬帝手上爆發成三次大規模征高句麗。就此役本身而言，其結局是一次以傾國之力換來的實質停戰：雙方都保住了核心地盤，高句麗贏得時間，隋朝則贏得一次對自身消耗能力的實測。
resultEn: As for the military result, the historical record contains no account of the Sui army taking the walled cities of Liaodong or Pyongyang in this campaign; the main body halted in the Jinxiang area, the offensive was halted by rain, by the men’s exhaustion and by the grain, and the concrete results were close to nothing. On the Goguryeo side, the defence commanded by Iji Winde and the diplomacy of King Go-won worked at the same time: the gesture of sending envoys to sue for peace and to acknowledge vassalage bought the withdrawal of the Sui army, and once that army was gone the frontier line returned to where it stood, leaving Goguryeo free to shift forces against the Turks to the north. Inside the Sui court the campaign stirred alarm, the commanders were detained and questioned for a time over a great labour spent for nothing, and were then put back into service because the frontier required them. After it the emperor no longer pressed east in a hurry, yet he did not abandon the preparations, and by the end of his reign the accumulated weight of state resources and of frontier trouble finally broke out under the Yangdi in the shape of three large-scale expeditions against Goguryeo. Taken on its own terms, the outcome of Jinxiang was an armed pause bought at the price of a national mobilisation: both sides kept their essential ground, Goguryeo bought time, and the Sui bought a measuring of its own capacity to bear such a war.
